title: U.S. House · Colorado's 6th District
area: Parts of the Denver metro area, including Aurora, Centennial and Highlands Ranch.

context.text: Incumbent Jason Crow (D) was unopposed in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary. Jason Ray Clark won the Republican primary. Ballotpedia's most recent race ratings (as of late September 2026) rate the district as Safe/Solid Democratic.

summary.text: Jason Crow is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 6th District, first elected in 2018. He is a former Army Ranger and attorney who represented veterans before entering politics, and he serves on the House Armed Services and Intelligence committees. His campaign materials emphasize lowering costs, national security, and ending dark money in politics.

background.text: Born in Madison, Wisconsin, in 1979. According to his official biography, he grew up in a working-class family, held minimum-wage jobs in high school, and enlisted in the National Guard and did construction work to help pay for school; he describes himself as the first in his family to graduate from college.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Wisconsin in 2002 and a law degree from the University of Denver in 2009.

Served in the U.S. Army from 2002 to 2006. His official biography says he served three tours in Iraq and Afghanistan with the 82nd Airborne Division and the 75th Ranger Regiment and received the Bronze Star.

After leaving the military, worked as an attorney helping Colorado veterans access benefits and care; his official biography says Denver named him its Pro-bono Lawyer of the Year. He also worked as an adjunct professor.
According to Wikipedia, he served on the Colorado Board of Veterans Affairs from 2009 to 2014 and became a partner at the law firm Holland & Hart.

First ran for Congress in 2018, defeating the Democratic primary opponent Levi Tillemann and then four-term Republican incumbent Mike Coffman in the general election, becoming the first Democrat to represent the district since it was created in 1983. He won re-election in 2020 and 2022.

Serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. He was an impeachment manager in the Senate trial held in 2020, and his official biography says he was the lead Democrat on the Joint Task Force on the Assassination of President Trump.
According to his official biography, he has a son and a daughter and lives in Colorado.

priorities.text: Working to build the clean energy economy to create good-paying jobs while mitigating some of the worst effects of climate change, expand access to entrepreneurial and small business resources in underserved areas, and build a talented workforce.
Working every avenue to bring down prices, address supply chain issues, and deliver relief on costs like health care, prescription drugs, housing, groceries, and energy.
Fighting to crack down on dark money in politics, strengthen ethics rules, and restore trust in government.

positions.summary: Says gun safety laws can reduce violent crime while protecting Second Amendment rights, and has introduced resolutions promoting safe firearm storage.
positions.quote: Enacting common-sense laws -- policies that are supported by a huge majority of Americans -- can help reduce violent crime and make our communities, schools, and homes safer.

positions.summary: Told CPR News that Congress needs to reinstate the enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies to help drive down health care costs.
positions.quote: We need to reinstate the ACA subsidies to help drive down costs

positions.summary: Says he is working to build the clean energy economy to create jobs while mitigating the worst effects of climate change.
positions.quote: Now Jason is working to build the clean energy economy to create good-paying jobs while mitigating some of the worst effects of climate change

positions.summary: Told CPR News he championed multiple Congressional War Powers Resolutions to end the war with Iran; cosponsored H.Con.Res. 93, directing the removal of U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran, and H.Con.Res. 68 on Venezuela.
Cosponsored H.R. 2743, the Raise the Wage Act of 2025 (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 12, the Women's Health Protection Act of 2025 (119th Congress).
Told CPR News that tariffs are hurting small businesses and supply chains, and said Congress needs to reassert its authority and end the tariff wars.
positions.quote: are destroying our small businesses, our supply chains, and increasing the cost of goods substantially

positions.summary: Told CPR News ICE must be reined in and that private companies should be banned from running immigration detention centers.
positions.quote: I think we should ban private companies from running these types of centers.

record.text: Serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence (Central Intelligence Agency and Open Source Intelligence subcommittees) and the House Committee on Armed Services (Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation; Intelligence and Special Operations subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.
Introduced a resolution designating June 21 as National ASK (Asking Saves Kids) Day to encourage secure firearm storage.
Introduced the SHINE Act, described by his office as legislation to crack down on dark money in politics.
Introduced the Honoring the Sacrifice of Troops in War Act, which he says would prevent the Secretary of Defense from manipulating government data on troop casualties.

candidates.name: Jason Ray Clark

summary.text: Jason Ray Clark is the Republican nominee for Colorado's 6th District, having advanced from the June 30, 2026 Republican primary with no other candidate on the ballot. According to BallotReady, he is a West Point graduate who founded an investment firm and a financial coaching business. His BallotReady profile lists public safety and the cost of living among his issues.

background.text: According to BallotReady, he graduated from Smoky Hill High School in 1988 and earned an engineering bachelor's degree from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1992.
According to BallotReady, he founded Clark Brothers Investments (2007-2023) and The Buffett Way Financial Coaching (2023-2025).
Advanced from the June 30, 2026 Republican primary for the 6th District as the only candidate on the ballot, with 38,437 votes.

priorities.text: Affordability: says addressing rising costs of rent, education and healthcare is his top priority.
Jobs across Colorado, including support for entrepreneurs, small business and developers.

positions.summary: Told CPR News he disagrees with President Trump's tariffs.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website and Ballotpedia 2026 survey list affordability, jobs and crime as priorities, with few specifics; the survey names limited government as a passion area. His tariffs position comes from CPR News. His Ballotpedia profile also lists a 2025 survey as a candidate for Colorado governor; it was not used.

candidates.name: Patty McMahon

summary.text: Patty McMahon is the Libertarian Party candidate for Colorado's 6th District. She describes a more than 30-year career at the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and says she is running as an independent voice outside partisan politics.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Bishop Gorman High School and a bachelor's degree from Metropolitan State University of Denver in 1989; her career experience includes working as a writer.

In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, she says she spent over three decades at the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, beginning as an investigator and later serving as Denver's Outreach & Education Coordinator and congressional liaison for 25 years.

Says she was selected as Region VIII Lead for the White House Initiative on Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians, and Pacific Islanders, and in 2004 was selected for a committee that reorganized the EEOC.

Says she serves on Colorado nonprofit and civic boards, has served as a campaign director and public relations director for congressional candidates from different parties, and has lived in the district for 26 years.

priorities.text: Defending constitutional limits on government power and the separation of powers.
Protecting civil liberties and due process.
Opposing unnecessary war and military intervention.

candidates.researchNotes: Libertarian. Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; it centers on separation of powers, civil liberties, war authorization and congressional oversight of federal spending (including a proposed TRUST Act). Few answers touch the guide's other listed issues, so depth stays minimal.

statements.quote: I oppose unnecessary military intervention because I believe war should always be a last resort, clearly justified, and constitutionally authorized.
statements.context: In her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.name: Samir Witta

summary.text: Samir Witta is an unaffiliated candidate for Colorado's 6th District. He is a physician who says he has practiced oncology in Colorado for 25 years and founded nonprofits aimed at helping patients with health costs. He says he is running on health care costs, housing affordability, and limiting the influence of large donors.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he came to the United States 27 years ago; his first job was at a gas station in Washington, D.C.

Earned an M.D. from Charles University in 1990 and a Ph.D. from the National Institutes of Health in 1995, and graduated from the University of Colorado in 2004; his career experience includes working as a physician.
Says he has practiced oncology in Colorado for 25 years and built his own clinic; says 5280 Magazine has named him a top oncologist in the Denver metro area four years running.
Says he founded nonprofits to cover patients' insurance premiums, assembled a team to erase deductibles for cancer patients, and started organizations supporting youth sports and education.

priorities.text: Healthcare reform: cap out-of-pocket deductibles and align drug prices with prices paid elsewhere.
Housing affordability: cap rent and HOA increases and rein in management companies.
Limiting the influence of mega-donors and corporations in Congress.

positions.summary: In his 2026 Ballotpedia survey, lists capping rent and HOA increases as a campaign message.

candidates.researchNotes: Independent. Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; no campaign website was checked beyond that. His answers do not directly take a side on most other listed issues.

candidates.name: Meredith Ryan

summary.text: Meredith Ryan is the Unity Party candidate for Colorado's 6th District. She has worked as a legal administrative assistant, social services program assistant, and paraprofessional, and holds a seminary degree. Her campaign messages in her Ballotpedia survey center on international law, campaign finance, and a Green New Deal.

background.text: Earned an associate degree from the College of Westchester in 1978, a bachelor's degree from Concordia College in 2006, and graduated from Princeton Theological Seminary in 2010.
Her career experience includes working as a legal administrative assistant, social services program assistant, and paraprofessional.
In her 2026 Ballotpedia survey, she says she has held board positions and roles in community organizations throughout her adult life.

priorities.text: Says the U.S. must adhere to international law and end complicity in what she describes as genocide in Gaza and the West Bank.
Calls for a Green New Deal.

statements.quote: The USA needs to offer a Green New Deal allowing for advancements in technologies without them being at the expense of working people and their work/career options.
statements.context: In her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.researchNotes: Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; no campaign website checked. Her answers do not state a position on military aid itself, so none was inferred.

Biographies for Jason Ray Clark rest on a BallotReady profile (no campaign site or news profile found); Patty McMahon, Samir Witta, and Meredith Ryan rely on their own Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey responses and are self-described.
